name: Vim
note: From Vim's own :help index (runtime/doc/index.txt, the source behind vimhelp.org/index.txt.html): section 1 Insert mode, section 2 Normal mode including its window (CTRL-W), square bracket, g and z sub-tables, section 3 Visual mode and section 4 Command-line editing. The mode is the context ("Normal", "Insert", "Visual", "Command-line"). Names are Vim's own action text from the index; where two commands share the same wording the keys are appended in parentheses to keep them apart. vim.rtorr.com was used only as a secondary cross-check of the common Normal-mode commands; every entry here comes from Vim's documentation. Vim is case-sensitive and this chord grammar upper-cases letters, so a capital-letter command is written as Shift plus the letter ("G" is Shift+G, "j" is J) and shifted punctuation as Shift plus the unshifted key on a US layout ("$" is Shift+4, "^" is Shift+6). Bindings are the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. Left out: section 5 Terminal-Job mode and section 6 EX commands (":" commands are typed lines, not chords); every command that takes an argument (d{motion}, f{char}, "{register}, m{A-Za-z}, /{pattern}<CR> and the like) - the optional register prefix ["x] is ignored, so dd, yy, p and x are present; all mouse bindings (<LeftMouse>, <MiddleMouse>, <RightMouse> and their modified forms); <NL> and <S-NL>, and the <Help> and <Undo> keys, which the grammar has no name for; and the entries Vim marks "not used" or "reserved for extensions".
